title: Bryan Johnson's evening routine: 9 protocols for 3-minute sleep onset
summary: Bryan explains how he falls asleep within 3 minutes nightly, ranking in the 99.4th sleep percentile. The routine centers on a noon final meal, HRV breathing, dim red/amber light, a 60-minute screen-free wind-down, and a consistent 8:30 pm bedtime, with advice to start small.

principles.text: Finish eating early; it's the single most impactful sleep change. Bryan's last meal is around noon.
principles.quote:
My final meal is around noon. That's ~8.5 hours before I sleep.

This is the single most impactful change I made.

principles.text: Eating near bed raises resting heart rate and cuts sleep quality; digestion conflicts with deep sleep.
principles.quote: When I eat close to bed, my resting heart rate before sleep climbs to 52-56 beats per min (bpm) and I lose roughly 30% of my sleep quality.

principles.text: Build up gradually: finish food 2, then 3, then 4 hours before bed, and check your data each morning.
principles.quote: Start by finishing food 2 hours before bed. Move to 3 hours. Then 4. Each step forward shows up in your data the next morning.

principles.text: Do 10 minutes of 4:6 breathing before bed to raise HRV and calm the nervous system.
principles.quote: I do 10 min of 4:6 breathing before bed. That's breathing in through the nose for 4 seconds and out for 6.

principles.text: Turn screens off 60 minutes before bed and wind down with family, walking, or reading a real book.
principles.quote: I turn off screens 60 min before bed and enable Sleep Bryan.

principles.text: Keep a consistent bedtime within +/- 30 minutes, timed to allow 7-9 hours of sleep.
principles.quote: Choose a time that allows you to get 7-9 hours of sleep. Go to bed within +/- 30 min of this time every night.
